column1: # One row per implementer PR, appended when the controller rules its review.
# Purpose: the tier guard cannot be answered inside one run — n is 2-3 PRs, ticket
# difficulty swamps the tier effect, and finding-counts are not comparable across
# PRs because selectDimensions trims the fan-out by diff profile. So accumulate
# instead of concluding.
# READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING ROWS. The dispatch rule bound class=routine to
# sonnet until it was REVERTED on 2026-08-16; since then every class dispatches
# at the session's tier (run-team/SKILL.md phase 2). Under the old rule class
# and tier moved together, so a routine-vs-correction split over the rows it
# produced measures class, not tier. That split cannot run over those rows
# anyway: every row dated before the revert is class=routine. The
# class=correction rows this file now holds are all post-revert, so they say
# nothing about the old rule.
# Only a same-class comparison across tiers is informative, and exactly one row
# was dispatched off the old binding while it was still in force — PR #480,
# routine at opus, the deliberate control. That is n=1 for the old rule, not a
# whole-file count of routine-at-opus rows and not a result; answering the tier
# question needs more of them, and after the revert they come from the session's
# own tier varying rather than from the class.
# Recount before citing any of this: an append lands a row without touching this
# header.
# closed_own_ticket  no  = review found a defect leaving this ticket's OWN stated
#                          acceptance criteria unmet, or reintroducing its defect
# minted_false_claim yes = the diff added a factual claim (comment/doc/test name)
#                          that measured false, beyond any inherited from the ticket
# run_date

REGRESSION in the payload the three tickets exist to make truthful: the new dirtyFiles awk emitted INVALID JSON for a staged rename, destroying the whole audit document including every other worktree's entry, where the $2 code it replaced emitted valid JSON. Found independently by 2 dimensions, 2-0 each. Minted: reap.sh's comment declared "$wt is never the main checkout" — measurably false, and it was the stated ground for a guard that then printed a false reason

FIRST same-class row at a non-sonnet tier — the control this file's header asks for. Met every acceptance criterion; caught a set -eu hazard its own edit created (git exits 1 in exactly the state the feature exists for, so an unguarded $() would abort the audit) and pinned the silent states with a literal after finding /unknown/ matches survived the mutation. Minted anyway: the new comment claimed "both permission cases are silent" — true of stash list, false of the show-ref call already in hand; and its state table named 3 unknown states where there are 4

met the ticket's own stated bar (it explicitly offered "asserting atRisk has no duplicate SHAs on the ordinary fixture" as sufficient) and the dedupe itself is correct — fix-deleted mutant reds. Review raised the bar above the ticket: 3 findings + 1 reversed refutation all said the TEST does not discriminate (uniq mutant survived 57/57, !seen[$2] survived 57/57, split itself unasserted). REGRESSION: shipped a guard that cannot fire — the SNAPSHOT_NONEMPTY probe ran AFTER the node_modules symlink, so a failed `git archive | tar -x` still reported pathVerified true in any repo that has node_modules, i.e. exactly the repos #140 exists for. Found by 2 dimensions, 2-0 each. Minted: the new test comment claimed `additionalProperties: false` + `required` "already caught the sibling defect at #113/#118, same schema" — #113 is resolveDimensions own hand-written REQUIRED array and #118 is stale test-count comments; neither is a JSON schema. TIER CAVEAT: dispatched at sonnet IN ERROR — the controller session loaded a SKILL.md from a checkout 57 commits stale, carrying the pre-revert phase-2 rule; under the rule in force this ticket would have run at session tier. Accidental sample, not a designed control.

FIRST minted_false_claim=no in this file (9 rows prior, all yes). Review ran 6/6 dims: 1 survived, 0 refuted, 3 unverified — and the ONLY survived finding was PRE-EXISTING code the diff never touched (no-undo-audit.sh:490 LC_ALL false safe, filed #582), not anything the PR asserted. Both in-scope suggestions were REFUTED by measurement, not waved through: the withSplitXargs docstring gap (the sentence the fix wanted already sat 4 lines above the caller, added by this same commit) and the "dead doesNotMatch" (4 discriminating mutants + 7 non-discriminating controls, incl. the finding own full revert which the sibling assert.match catches alone — 4th refutation of that claim class here after #573/#562/#568-6, filed #587/#588 as records). Implementer discipline is the likely cause of the no: it could NOT measure GNU xargs (docker hung), so it kept the 123/124/125/126/127 mapping OUT of the diff, marked it documented-only in the PR body, and rewrote that body after CI when its first draft restated those numbers as if measured. It also proved the path had ZERO prior coverage by instrumenting the guard with a marker file and running origin/main suite (66 tests, marker never written) rather than assuming. Fix-applier outcome: no-op, HEAD unchanged, 811/811.

Pinned that verify-sha fetch guard is FATAL. Ticket was verified live by the controller in phase 0 (mutant survived 9/9 even after PR #565 added fetch tests). Implementer went beyond the ticket: swept EVERY die guard in the file one at a time and found two more with the same unpinned-fatality hole (:27, :35) — reported rather than widened, filed #580. Its assertion choice beat the controller-suggested one: doesNotMatch(/origin\/main tip =/) pins PROGRESS PAST the guard, so it does not couple to which downstream guard fires or how it is worded, and that trace line is already pinned verbatim by the healthy-run test so it cannot go vacuous unseen. Review (3 dims, size-tier trim) 0 survived / 2 refuted 2-0 / 2 unverified. Minted: the new fixture comment claimed a bad URL and a removed remote are "byte-identical here" — that is the PRE-#565 defect; the same file asserts the opposite at :180-181 and the suite is green, so provably false. Caught by a SUGGESTION with zero refuters while a CRITICAL finding on the same line attacked the citation number and was correctly refuted 2-0. Fix-applier reworded (conclusion kept, stale reason dropped) and correctly left the neighbouring PAST-TENSE historical record alone.

Unknown-flag sweep, makeSweep(die) in arg.mjs across 4 scripts. Review: 6/6 dims, 16 findings, 2 survived / 3 refuted / 11 unverified. Implementer corrected its own brief (candidates.mjs already covered by parseArgs/#173; migrating would WEAKEN it since candidates takes no positionals while board build|serve are exactly that shape) and caught its own vacuous pin mid-mutation (unit probe called arg() before sweep(), so --base=main died in arg() either way). Minted TWO: PR body "up from 813" (measured origin/main baseline is 810 — controller re-measured from a clean git archive extract, 43 test files; two siblings independently confirmed 810), and board.mjs:411 comment naming serve()/gather() as imported by board.test.mjs when only createBoardServer is (survived 2-0). Controller ruled a MUTUAL EXCLUSION the refuters could not see (unverified-2 vs the upheld refutation of refuted-2 cannot both land) and REVERSED a 1-1 split (diff-stats.mjs:143 clause "imported by review-pr snapshot path" is false — review-pr.js invokes it as a CLI subprocess). Fix-applier refuted 3 by mutation, declined 2, recorded them as band-records #589/#595 rather than actionable tickets.

prove-merge stderr-swallow + false cause assertion, both guards (:55 rev-parse --quiet and :58 cat-file 2>/dev/null), mirroring PR #565. SECOND minted_false_claim=no of this file, and like #576 the cause looks like refusal-to-assert-what-was-not-measured: implementer re-measured the healthy-path stderr for THIS script rather than inheriting #565 figure (896 bytes/13 lines, all the scripts own trace, 0 from git, identical before and after), and REFUTED its own ticket claim that prove-merge was the last instance of the class — sweeping up five more sites, filed #578. Review 6/6 dims, 0 survived / 0 refuted / 7 unverified (all suggestion = zero refuters by policy, so NONE was checked by the review). One finding was an artifact of an incomplete read: it flagged the rev-parse change as unauthorized, but the authorization is in a #566 COMMENT the specialist never fetched (gh issue view --json title,body drops comments). Fix-applier then re-read its OWN added comments literally and found 2 of 3 wrong, fixing them in a follow-up commit rather than --amend to avoid a force-push stranding the CI monitor on a cancelled run.

Empty-catch silent misclassification in board.mjs. Review 6/6 dims, 0 survived / 3 refuted (ALL 1-1 splits) / 8 unverified. Controller REVERSED two refutations: refuted[1]+refuted[2]+unverified[0] were ONE type-blindness defect found by three independent dimensions, and both refutations rested on 'no producer' from a grep over skills/fleet that CANNOT see the writer — sidecars are harness-written, outside this repo. Minted: the new 16-line comment at :208-211 promised the {} fallback prevents a token-drop, while a null sidecar measurably drops the agent's tokens, counts it skipped, and blames the .jsonl transcript — the implementer rejected 'throw e' for exactly that outcome, then left a path producing it. Fix-applier applied a shape guard making the comment true, and caught a second minted claim of its own (changed 'unreadable' to 'unusable' because a null sidecar reads fine). Its own new warn-once dedupe was unpinned — impl mutated the message wording, never the Set gate. Finisher found TWO deferrals the PR body promised ('Separate ticket.' twice) and never filed: #605, #606. Deferred+filed 5 total: #602 #603 #604 #605 #606.

gone() ancestor walk never reached /, three byte-identical copies. Review 6/6 dims, 1 survived (2-0, mutation-proved) / 1 refuted 2-0 / 8 unverified. THIRD minted_false_claim=no in this file: the comments dimension produced only a missing-version-tag finding, refuted, and its refuter verified the underlying git-behaviour claim TRUE against git 2.50.1 — no added assertion was false. Implementer had already widened from the ticket's 2 named callers to all 4, and built gone-walk.test.mjs because the ticket's REJECTED variant passes all 101 caller-level tests. The review then found that test disabled itself: its root guard skipped the whole 9-row matrix, so under stubbed uid 0 the rejected variant was 101/98/0/3 fully green. Fix-applier repaired it (now red on exactly gone "", skipped 3->2) and its refuters sharpened two more: a shadow gone() mid-file carrying the rejected form measured 832/832 green before the extract() fix, and unverified[2]'s own suggested_fix was BROKEN as written (existsSync not imported; would red the suite and leak a 0o000 dir). 4 findings refuted by measurement, filed as wontfix records #607-#610; #391 commented rather than duplicated.

LC_ALL=C locale pin, false-safe rebase verdict. Review: 6/6 dims, 19 findings, 7 survived (5 critical) / 1 refuted 1-1 / 11 unverified. Minted, and this is the signature: the SWEEP pasted its own 13-line justifying comment into five scripts and the tool inventory was FALSE in four — derive-testcmd has one grep and no tr/sed/awk; worktree-audit has only awk+paste and its own next line says 'both parsed by awk'; reap has no sed and its tr/grep read git cherry output not ignored-file names; inflight has no grep BY DESIGN its own older comments explain. Fifth error in the same block named the wrong tr as failing. Also shipped 'zero POSIX classes' in six comments + the PR body + a saved team memory, while no-undo-audit.sh:240 has [![:space:]] 215 lines below the comment denying it. survived[5] is the one that mattered most: the PR's own regression test could not discriminate 'export LC_ALL=C' from 'LC_ALL=C', because the test pre-seeded LC_ALL into the child env and POSIX keeps the export attribute — so #582's fix was unpinned by its own test, and CI (Linux/GNU tr) could not fail either way. Fix-applier fixed both, and FALSIFIED a review finding by measurement: BSD paste -sd truncates its whole output at the bad byte at exit 0 while awk is locale-immune, so worktree-audit's pin is load-bearing for paste, not awk — review's per-script table was wrong and it corrected the PR body. Its decisive control: old env + export-mutant = 69/69 green, reproducing the defect. Deferred #611-#614 + #583 comment; controller filed #615 from the finisher's dedupe-guard caveat.

json.sh extraction, 9 scripts building JSON by hand + jstr triplicated. Review: 6/6 dims, 26 findings, 11 survived (4 critical) / 2 refuted / 13 unverified, 33 agents. The implementer's headline was overriding the TICKET's own decided remedy on measurement: #119 prescribed guarding the source with '|| die', but '.' is a POSIX special builtin so a failed open aborts before || runs (controller reproduced: /bin/sh rc=1, dash rc=2, both with the guard UNFIRED; bash rc=0 fired). Scripts are #!/bin/sh and exit 1 from inflight.sh means TAKEN, so the ticket's own remedy would fabricate a claim on a free ticket. Shipped [ -r ] first and pinned that mutant. Minted, and the review found a CAUSAL CHAIN not a list: the new comment 'This script has no exit-1 verdict to fabricate' is false in BOTH scripts it was added to, and that false belief is why four jarr sites were left without the || die the other 14 got — diff-introduced, since this PR's json.sh is what made those helpers able to fail, turning a broken stage into exit 1 (= REFUSED dirty worktree) with zero stdout and no diagnostic on a worktree just logged clean. Also minted: json.sh 'the six that do pin it' (8 callers, 5 pin), header 'three callers read exit 1 as a verdict' (five), and 'nothing in POSIX sh can catch a syntax error, so the suite covers it instead' — wrong twice. A refuter incidentally falsified the TICKET's own measured comment that only $branch was reachable: a quote is legal in a ref name, so git cat-file -e resolves 'evil"tag' and $sha reaches the payload unparseable at exit 0 (controller reproduced; the review's own unverified[2] would have trimmed the wrap that prevents it). unverified[9] explains the run's recurring defect: the guard blocks were 68%% byte-identical across callers and 13-for-13 between two of them, which is how one false sentence reached two files. Deferred #617 (dirtyFiles C-quoting, different field from the ticket's table) + #618 record.

reap.sh worktree-remove refusal read off the exit code, git's reason discarded. Review 6/6 dims, 2 survived (both important, both 2-0, SAME defect from correctness+silent-failure) / 2 refuted / 7 unverified. Minted, and it is THIS TICKET'S OWN DEFECT CLASS reintroduced by its fix: #391 exists because 'the reason names the last step, not the failure', and the fix shipped a reason asserting a FILESYSTEM state produced by a probe that reads the REGISTRY. Both phrases measured false in reachable shapes — 'still on disk' in the ordinary concurrent-reap race the script's own header documents AND where reap's own gone() established absence four lines earlier; 'nothing was removed' after the whole worktree directory was deleted. Both new tests stayed green with the false claim in place (symlink shape only). Controller overrode the review's preferred remedy: it offered drop-the-clause OR gate-on-a-stat, and the Agent Brief forbids the stat outright ('a third probe here would make that worse'). Second minted claim: '#83 is already open' — #83 is CLOSED (controller verified the title matches, so the finding's wrong-ticket claim was correctly refuted; only the state was wrong). Implementer had widened scope to a third site and flagged it reversible; the fix-applier MEASURED it as a genuine control-flow change (a [gone] branch with no worktree was REAPED pre-fix), reverted it, and filed #622. Finisher found an unbacked promise in the rewritten body and filed #634, then proved it worse than the body framed: %(refname:short) under a same-named tag emits heads/<name>, which both breaks branch -D and silently stands down the entire worktree guard block. Deferred #622 #625-#630 + #634.

release-ticket.sh done_wt recorded the exit code, not what landed. Review 6/6 dims, 3 survived (1 critical) / 5 refuted (TWO of them 1-1 splits, one critical) / 8 unverified. Minted: the PR CONTRADICTED ITSELF — occupied()'s new doc-comment said 'git worktree remove against a symlink standing in for the dir deletes the target THROUGH the link and returns 0' while its own table 10-24 lines below said 'rc 255, registration CLEARED, path kept'. Controller reproduced rc=255 on the cited git. Provenance, found by the fix-applier and the best result of the wave: the rc-0 number was REAL but taken on a DIFFERENT shape — a symlink POINTING AT the registered dir gives rc 0 with the link left DANGLING, and that shape is precisely what justifies [ -L ] because -e is then false. The controller's own ruling (and the reviewer's suggested fix) would have collapsed the justification onto the rc-255 shape where -e alone answers, leaving -L unexplained; the fix-applier kept both shapes and corrected only the mislabelling, then swept with grep + git log -S to prove nothing else inherited it. Both 1-1 splits settled by controller measurement, both UPHOLDING the refuters: the critical one claimed a truncated listing reads as a cleared registration, but the survivor is an EMPTY husk with no gitdir file that git worktree prune itself calls removable — so 'Released' was accurate and the proposed fix would have reported Indeterminate over a completed removal; the other manufactured its state by running claim-ticket from a subdirectory, which SKILL.md forbids. Implementer had earlier OVERTURNED its own brief's instruction to make gone() tri-valued, correctly — gone()'s contract already prescribes the pairing, and controller verified gone() byte-identical across revs with a positive control. Deferred #631-#633; controller filed #623 #624 from the declared-left list.

rebase-check-refresh jobs-API failure misreported as a missing job. Review 3/6 dims (correctness+tests+comments, size trim), dimensionsUnrun=[], 1 survived (tests/important, 2-0) / 1 refuted (2-0) / 1 unverified (suggestion). NO minted claim: the only candidate was the "~20 lines earlier" comment, refuted unanimously — both refuters established it narrates the CI WALK (the runs query — rebase-check-refresh.yml's `RUNS_JSON=$(gh api "repos/$GH_REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?...")` assignment — sits ~30 lines above the same file's `.github/scripts/rerun-rebase-check.sh "$PR" "$SHA" "$BEHIND_BY" $RUN_IDS` invocation; cited by construct rather than line number so an edit to that workflow cannot stale them again), not the test file layout. Implementer re-derived and found the defect RELOCATED into .github/scripts/rerun-rebase-check.sh (a757d0a/0e5c38d) — ticket described the inline run: block; judged a stale snippet shape, not a contradicted criterion, correctly. Picked exit 6 over 5 deliberately: the suite uses jq own 5 to pin that an unroutable status fails the step, so routing 5 would have silently disarmed that test. Survived finding was a COVERAGE gap not a code defect — the JOBS_ERRS>0 branch must stay gated behind FOUND_JOB unset, and a found-and-rejected-with-sibling-error case was untested; specialist tried 8 other mutations of changed lines (all caught) plus an equivalent mutant -gt 0 -> -ne 0 (correctly stayed green), so the suite is not brittle. fix-pr-656 applied it with kill + negative control, read the pinned string off the tree per the controller cross-finding hazard (survived[0] pins "every candidate run rejected" which the declined unverified[0] would have reworded). Controller ruled unverified[0] no-apply/no-file: its OWN remedy says leave as is, boundary documented at sh:56-58, operator still sees per-run ::error:: + SKIPPED warning, #239 repriced bar. 952/952. Zero deferrals.

release-ticket.test.mjs permission fixtures: failure-safe restore + euid-0 guard. Review 3/6 dims (correctness+tests+comments), dimensionsUnrun=[], 1 survived (tests/important 2-0) / 2 refuted / 3 unverified. closed_own_ticket YES but via a MEASURED DEVIATION from the ticket: #184 prescribed guarding JSON.parse inside release(), and impl-184 measured that guard swallows a parse failure into json:null which nine assert.equal(json,null) cases read as refused-before-mutation — with the prescribed guard a die()-prints-garbage mutation went GREEN (regression missed), so the ticket own remedy would have built the second masking layer the ticket exists to complain about. Restored search bits in repo() t.after instead, leaving release() and its ~50 call sites untouched. Implementer also re-counted the fixture set: SIX not the 3/5/10 in the thread (controller dispatch-time count of 10 was 5 chmod calls + 5 comment mentions), including one chmod 0o644 invisible to any 0o000 grep. minted_false_claim YES, three in the comment block: sibling guards stated as fifteen (measured 14; the 15th occurrence is the comment QUOTING the literal string, and this file own guards use geteuid so it contributes zero), a POSITIONAL reference the test at the end of this file (test at 1809 of 2077, 11 tests follow, and run-team correction discipline bans positional refs), and after the fix commit added a SEVENTH EUID0 skip site the block still said six in five places (filed #661, shipped deliberately as prose-only). TWO CONTROLLER REVERSALS out of the refuted band, both correct: the positional one was a 1-1 split, the fifteen one was refuted 2-0 by BOTH refuters and both were wrong. Review suggested_fix for the survived finding was NOT implementable (a body that throws IS a failing test and node drops the teardown error) — fix-applier inverted the construction via a stand-in t collecting the after-callback, mutation kill 79/78/1 single failure plus behaviour-preserving negative control green. Deferred #660 (inflight.test.mjs same class, re-measured as SEVEN fixtures not the finding six, 0 guards, rm -rf teardowns cannot remove a 0o000 dir as non-root). 950/950.

review-and-fix.md pointer/target mismatch — a literal search for a pointer found only the pointer. Review 3/6 dims, dimensionsUnrun=[], 1 survived (correctness/important 2-0) / 0 refuted / 2 unverified (both in scope, both refuted-into-survival). NO minted claim: the doc fix drew ZERO findings; all three findings were against the PIN the implementer volunteered, not the correction itself. THE PIN GREENED ON ITS OWN TICKETS DEFECT — with both targets reverted and both pointer verbs reworded the pre-PR test file read 3/3/0 GREEN, i.e. the full #197 document state passed. Cause: every bold span the CLAUSE regex did not recognise as a pointer was registered as a TARGET, so a pointer resolved to another POINTER. impl-197 had built that pin deliberately to stop citation rot, ran a six-row mutation matrix with two negative controls, and still shipped it — the third instance of this class in the repo. Fixed by scanning block-leading emphasis only. TWO further review remedies were themselves wrong: the suggested CLAUSE regex over-matches (a bare space becomes sufficient to continue a list, falsely pinning an adjacent **and** stress emphasis — measured 7/6/1 RED on benign prose) and the fix-applier shipped a narrower one after re-verifying the refuters claim itself; and a refuter SHARPENED the vacuity finding beyond its own evidence, showing a SINGLE see->consult reword retires a pin at 5/5/0 with targets untouched. PINNED=5 re-derived from the post-edit tree, not copied. Finisher spot-checked by running: baseline 6/6/0, pre-PR doc 6/3/3 RED, single-verb reword 5/4/1 RED with the test count dropping as the retired pointer stops generating its pin. Incident: the fix-appliers mutation driver used a RELATIVE path and wrote three mutations into the MAIN checkout (harness resets cwd between Bash calls); self-caught, repaired surgically with git show HEAD:path so the two unrelated dirty files survived, whole matrix re-run. Zero deferrals.

rebase-check-refresh.yml: three accounting holes exiting green having evaluated nothing. Review 3/6 dims, dimensionsUnrun=[], 3 survived (1 correctness + 2 tests, all 2-0) / 2 refuted (BOTH 1-1 SPLITS) / 2 unverified. THE FIX FOR exit-green-saying-nothing INTRODUCED exit-red-saying-nothing: the new guard used jq length, which is not an array check (null->0, object->key count, string->char count), so null/object/string never reached its message and died at the UNGUARDED bare assignment on the next line — jq exit 5, no ::error::, no summary — the exact pattern that same block comments against twelve lines earlier. TWO CONTROLLER REVERSALS from the refuted band: refuted[0] framing correctly refuted (step does end red, via the downstream assertion) but its DEFECT upheld and applied — empty gh stdout leaves N empty, both readers log [: : integer expected and read FALSE, so this PR headline cross-check is inoperative on that input and FINDING 1 remedy does NOT close it (member independently confirmed); refuted[1] subsumed by FINDING 1, no file. CONTROLLER LEAN REFUTED AND WITHDRAWN — I proposed adding MALFORMED to the counter set so one bad row stays a warning; the refuter measured that this REOPENS the hole #162 exists to close (all-malformed returns to exit 0 with a zeros summary) and turns #162 own acceptance test red 957/958, and that the ticket literal formula fails a single malformed row exactly as shipped code does, so my broader-than-asked premise was false too. Filed as #665 needs-triage with the refutation and a wontfix recommendation. Ordering ruling paid off: the parse-guard test was written LAST off the post-fix tree, which had grown from ONE annotation to THREE, so a pin copied from the finding text would have been stale. Member also pinned the projection guard FINDING 1 introduced — a fourth guard shipping with no witness. Finisher verified by EXECUTION: 13-row annotation matrix over the lifted step, no input died without an annotation, [] still exits 0. Controller ruled the degraded-[] ceiling NOT filable (no remedy available from inside the step). 962/962.

review-path-default.test.mjs: four unpinned invariants of the default review path. Review 3/6 dims, dimensionsUnrun=[], 1 survived (comments/important 2-0) / 0 refuted / 2 unverified (both in scope, both survived refutation). Ticket arrived PARTLY STALE and the implementer sorted it per-item: item 1 asked to pin SEVEN field names, the tree had EIGHT (dimensionsUnrun added later); item 2 the controller hypothesised was already done and the implementer DISPROVED that by slice measurement — :90 slices Reviewers from 645 while the naming rule sits at :34, so the existing assertion covered a DIFFERENT occurrence and the rule had no pin at all. minted_false_claim YES: the shipped comment claimed to be the one claim in this file with a machine on the other side of it, made FALSE BY ITS OWN DIFF, which added an import of compute-board.mjs twenty lines later and whose own later comments call that the machine consumer. The pins were also both too brittle and too strict: two (fallback path) pins matched a literal space against raw hard-wrapped prose so a PURE REFLOW reds them (swept 55-120, only <=60 fires), and an absolute doesNotMatch ban on the fallback member name reds on a LEGITIMATE additive row the docs sanction. The reviews prescribed ===2 remedy was a lateral move (reds on a fourth default-path row) so the fix-applier shipped a measured FLOOR >=2 instead, which also closed a false negative the old ban left open: a row DELETED outright was green. Widened audit found only that one pin carried the reflow defect. Finisher verified all nine cells plus CONTROLS against the pre-fix tree, and hit the reflow trap in its own VERIFICATION — grep read 0 because the qualifier wrapped mid-phrase. Deferred #667 (the return-shape pin misses a field on a SHARED line, measured 15/15 silent miss). 958/958.

review-pr.js:134 stated tier rule contradicted its own table — claimed refuters are per-DIMENSION when the budget is keyed on SEVERITY. Review 6/6 dims (no trim, src+tests diff), dimensionsUnrun=[], 1 survived (comments/important 2-0) / 1 refuted (2-0, correctly) / 7 unverified. minted_false_claim NO, and the implementer is why: it settled every restated clause by evaluating the real constructs with comments STRIPPED FIRST, so the comment it was writing could not satisfy its own assertions, and it WEAKENED three claims rather than ship them — dropped a would-be-self-falsifying "only site that reads it" claim (writing it adds a third grep hit), wrote "directs" not "forces" because the findings schema enum still permits critical/important, and dropped the literal refuter count 2 because verifiers = A.verifiers || 2 is a DEFAULT an arg can override. The refuted finding was refuted correctly on CAUSATION: it framed the spec drift as something this PR broke, when the spec was already wrong — the real half survived separately and was applied. The survived finding was doc drift the diff INTRODUCED a pointer to: SIZE_TIER_DIMS still argued the retired faces-refuters framing while the new block cross-referenced it as "the same reason".
